subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add a core pace-aware provider usage contract for autonomous agents, and should the first implementation stop at observability or include opt-in throttling?
rationale: The remaining work adds provider-specific usage semantics, persisted state, new config, session/status output, and autonomous throttling behavior; source inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the product boundary or safe default.

options.title: Observability First
options.body: Capture and expose pace context in status and session_status without blocking work until the data model and provider semantics prove reliable.

options.title: Opt-In Enforcement
options.body: Add disabled-by-default thresholds that can throttle subagents or non-interactive work, with explicit config, tests, and recovery guidance.

options.title: Plugin/API First
options.body: Keep core lean by first designing generic provider and agent hooks so a plugin can own pace policy without hardcoding Anthropic behavior in core.

recommendation.title: Observability First
recommendation.body: Capture and expose pace context in status and session_status without blocking work until the data model and provider semantics prove reliable.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined product-scoping and provider usage/status history for this decision surface.
